newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Thursday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 2.111 billion yuan from 2.254 billion yuan with the 60-day contract the most actively traded.
Trading was less active than Wednesday with state banks reducing their activities, traders said.

Trading was also less active on the first-tier market this week than in the past few weeks due to a lack of market-moving news, they said. Head offices of state banks and short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank trade on the first-tier market.
Short-term financial centres in Beijing and Shanghai were net lenders in recent trading while the Guangdong financial centre was the biggest net borrower, they said.

On the second-tier market, where non-bank financial institutions including securities houses trade through the centres, trading was active partly due to Beijing's recent measures to standardise the state debt repurchase market.
The measures have pushed more funds into the interbank market from the repo market, traders said.
Traders said that with the end-of-the-month settlement date approaching, trading would be more active over the next few days on the first-tier market with the interbank rates gaining support.
